The Federal Reserve (Fed) influences borrowing costs, savings returns, and overall financial conditions across the [economy](https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/economic-recovery-status.html). At its [June 17 meeting](https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/federal-reserve-interest-rate.html), the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) held its target federal funds interest rate in the 3.50%-3.75% range, a decision investors broadly expected. The decision kept the Fed in a patient but [inflation](https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/investing-insights/how-does-inflation-affect-investments.html)-focused policy stance. Shelter costs increased 3.4% over the year, but slower home-price and rent growth may still help cool official inflation readings over time.[1](https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/federal-reserve-tapering-asset-purchases.html#footnote_region_6c83). The unemployment rate stood at 4.3% in May, and weekly initial jobless claims remained low at 228,000 in the week ending June 5.[2](https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/federal-reserve-tapering-asset-purchases.html#footnote_region_38c6). The Fed recently announced it would reduce regular purchases, and its bond holdings now stand near $6.7 trillion after peaking near $9 trillion in 2022.[3](https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/federal-reserve-tapering-asset-purchases.html#footnote_region_14e). # How The Federal Reserve Monetary Policy Can Impact Your Investments. The Federal Reserve has the power to influence the performance of stocks, bonds and other investments. Read more about the impacts of The Fed monetary policy. The Federal Reserve holds a lot of power when it comes to influencing the economy, and by proxy, the performance of stocks, bonds and other investments. With that in mind, it’s important to be aware of how changes to domestic monetary policy could impact your portfolio and the actions you can take to help safeguard your investments. The role of The Fed is to determine monetary policy to help encourage employment, manage inflation and control interest rates, all in an effort to drive sustainable economic growth. You can think of The Fed’s monetary policy like a game of tug of war. These are intended to slow the growth of the economy and help limit the rate of inflation.
